proposalEditorIssues: CORRECTNESS, confirmed by automated probe: switching slides or packages leaves the previous one's values in the fields. ProposalEditor renders SectionEditor and VariantEditor with no key, and both use uncontrolled defaultValue inputs plus useState(s.theme) / useState(v.featured) that never re-initialise. Measured: slides 03 through 09 all show slide 02's Title 'Where you are now' and Eyebrow 'THE SITUATION' while the heading above correctly reads the real slide title; the theme toggle reads Light on slide 05 which is Dark and on slides 03 and 07 which are Feature; packages 'Considered' and 'Full harvest' both show Essential's Name and CTA 'Accept Essential'. Screenshot: C:\Users\Work\Projects\tahi-dashboard\.claude\qa\inv-shots\ed-proposal-package.png shows the FAQ slide 08 with slide 04's fields. Fix is key={section.id} / key={variant.id}, or lift to controlled state.
CORRECTNESS: the package Currency Select is inert. It is hardcoded to value="NZD" with onChange={() => {}}, so a non-NZD package cannot be authored and the control misreports v.currency.
CORRECTNESS: NewProposalPanel tracks pick (blank versus template) and orgId in state, but onCreate(title.trim()) discards both. The template picker and the client selector are decoration.
CORRECTNESS: the rich-text toolbar buttons (B, I, list, link) have no onClick handler; the body is a bare textarea with a placeholder.

CORRECTNESS: every structural action is a toast only. Add a slide, Add a package, Add a step, Add a question, Add a comparison, Add a line and every Remove just call notify(). Nothing mutates the proposal, so the mini preview can never move.

MISSING: no slide reordering. The rail list has no drag handle and no move up or down, and no per-slide duplicate or delete. Delete exists only for the whole proposal. Ordering is the single most-used action in any deck editor.
MISSING: no slide-type picker. The data model already supports value_anchor, process, faq and untyped prose, each with a distinct editor, but 'Add a slide' cannot choose which.

MISSING: live preview is thin and in the wrong place. The 'How it reads' mini render exists only on the Cover slide and, because the fields are uncontrolled, it never reflects typing. Section and package slides get no preview at all. Preview is a full shell swap to view-proposal that discards the editor, with no width or device toggle and no scroll-sync to the slide being edited.

MISSING: pricing is one flat form. One-off, monthly and a free-text notes box. There is no deposit or instalment schedule, no discount, no GST or tax line, no total or twelve-month value roll-up even though the list computes one, and no compare-table preview despite the editor copy promising 'each one a row in the compare table'.

MISSING: no versioning. Publish and the 'Unpublished edits' pill imply a snapshot model, but there is no version list, no diff of what changed since the client last read it, no restore, and no record of which version each acceptance was made against. For a document that gets signed off, that is the gap that matters most.

MISSING: sharing is thin. The rail gives Copy, Open, Rotate and Revoke on one workspace-wide link. No per-recipient links, no per-viewer identification, no view-notification setting, no expiry reminder, no passcode, and 'Email link' fires straight to a toast with no compose step or subject line.
MISSING: no internal layer. No private notes on a slide, no reviewer or approve-before-send step, no comment threads, so Staci cannot review a deck before Liam sends it.

MISSING: the client's side of the conversation is one-way. Acceptances land in DecisionsPane, but there is no way to see the version the client was looking at when they accepted, and Reply is a toast rather than a thread.
MISSING: Reading analytics is only reachable from inside the editor. The list shows a per-row views bar but cannot open the analytics pane directly.
DESIGN: the editor's nav rail is on the RIGHT at 336px while every list rail is on the LEFT at 232px, with different section headers, item styling and count styling. Two rail idioms in one product.

DESIGN: BuilderHead packs back link, title, two or three pills, saving state and up to five actions into one row. At 1120 with a long title plus Publish, Preview and the More menu it is the densest header in the app and has no overflow rule.
DESIGN, mobile: the rail collapses behind a 'Slides and packages' toggle that replaces the body instead of sliding over it, so opening the outline loses your place in the slide you were editing.

WHAT LIAM LIKELY EXPECTS, in priority order: fix the stale-field bug and make the fields real; drag-reorder plus duplicate plus delete per slide; an 'Add a slide' type picker driven by the existing four types; a persistent live preview pane at the client's width, scroll-synced to the slide being edited, with a phone toggle; a real pricing model (deposit or instalments, discount, GST, totals, twelve-month value) with a compare-table preview; a template picker that actually seeds the deck, and 'Save as a template' round-tripping; versions with a published-versus-draft diff and a restore, and each acceptance stamped with the version it was made against; per-recipient share links with open notifications and an expiry reminder; and an internal notes plus review step before send.
results.proposedStandard:
"PART A, ONE HEADLINE BAND.

Name it HeadBand, ship it once in a shared kit, then delete sp-band, sa-flow, ops-kpis, pf-vitals, pm-tiles, ops-portal-strip and the invoices-studio Tiles. Keep sa-clientspine as its own thing: it is a progress spine, not a KPI band, and it is already consistent.

Position. Always directly under the page head and above the toolbar or rail. Never below the fold. Standardise the page head first: one PageHead at one height, title 1.5rem, one-line sub, actions right, so the band always starts at the same y. Today there are eight head heights between 49 and 106px.

Container. One bordered box, 1px hairline dividers between tiles, standard radius (leaf radius stays on CTAs and avatar wrappers only), overflow hidden. Borders not shadows, never a border on one side. This is the sp-band and ops-kpis model; the gapped-card model is dropped.

Count. Exactly four tiles. Three only where a page genuinely has three (portal Invoices). Never five or six. Proposals goes six to four by folding Draft plus Out to read into one 'In flight' tile and Declined plus Closed into 'Closed'. Deals drops from five to four.

Grid. Fixed 1.35fr 1fr 1fr 1fr at desk, not auto-fit, so the lead tile is visibly the lead and the count never changes with width.

Tile anatomy, top to bottom, one ramp everywhere. (1) Label: 12px icon plus text, 700/.625rem, .06em tracking, uppercase, --text-faint, one line, never wraps. (2) Figure: 700/1.375rem, tabular-nums, --text or the domain accent, one line. (3) Sub-line: 500/.6875rem, --text-muted, clamped to two lines. (4) Optional action: at most one, right-aligned inside the lead tile only, a text link in the accent colour, never a filled button. Fixed min-height 5.25rem so a re-wrapping sub-line cannot change band height, which is what makes Deals grow from 136 to 149px between 1440 and 1120.

Lead tile treatment. First tile only. Fill of --bg-secondary, or the domain accent's soft fill where the page has an accent; figure steps up to 1.625rem; an optional 2px accent meter under the sub-line when the figure has a denominator (capacity used, week elapsed, pipeline weighted). No accent rule on the other three, which kills the sa-flow-rule that currently paints all six tiles equally and leaves nothing reading as the lead.

Domain accent. Exactly one per page, from the existing four (money green, work slate, growth gold, time teal) plus danger. The accent tints the lead fill and the lead figure only. Non-lead tiles stay neutral unless a tile is in a genuine alarm state, which may take the danger tint. Keep the Time 'Unpriced' behaviour: it is the one place this already works.

Interaction. All four tiles are filters or none of them are. Never mixed. Today Proposals has a non-clickable lead sitting beside four aria-pressed neighbours that look identical, which breaks the visible-equals-permitted, clickable-equals-allowed invariant. Recommendation: bands are read-only and filtering lives in the rail, so there is one filter surface. Where a tile is genuinely a shortcut it gets a chevron and moves the rail's saved view rather than holding its own state.

The dark feature tile. Reserved for a page with exactly one thing a person is meant to do next. Two pages qualify: portal Overview (pf-needs, already dark, keep it) and Calls (sp-upnext, currently pale green, promote it to dark). A page with a dark feature tile does not also carry a four-tile band above it; the band moves below the tile, which portal Overview already does correctly. No other page gets one.

Breakpoints, container-query driven so a collapsed sidebar does not change the answer. At or above 68rem: four across, one row. 44 to 68rem: 2x2 with the lead tile spanning both columns of the first row. Below 44rem: 2x2, no span, figure 1.25rem, sub-line clamped to one line, band height under 170px. Never a horizontal scroller; Proposals is one today with no fade or edge affordance. The 170px ceiling is what rules out five and six tiles: Deals currently eats 429px above the board at 375.

Skeleton. Same box, same four cells, same min-height, so nothing jumps on arrival. The FlowSkeleton idea, with the fixed count.

Dark. The lead fill must be the accent mixed at roughly 14 percent against --bg, not the ~5 percent sa-flow uses, which is invisible in dark and leaves the Proposals lead tile indistinguishable from its neighbours. Every band ships with a dark check.

Pages that must gain a band. Requests (open, triage, overdue, due this week), Tasks (assigned to me, due this week, overdue, blocked), Clients (retainers, at risk, MRR, onboarding). These are the three most-used studio pages and the three with no headline at all.

PART B, THE RAIL CONTRACT.

One RailLayout in the shared kit, imported by every list page. Delete the three copies in requests-toolbar.jsx, tasks.jsx and clients-kit.jsx, and the near-misses pa-nrail in portal-account.jsx and inv-views in invoices-studio-kit.jsx.

Geometry. aside.rail on the LEFT, 232px fixed, no border box, no side border, sticky under the page head with its own scroll. Main column minmax(0,1fr).

Sections, in this order, always. (1) VIEWS: 'All <nouns>' first with the total, then the saved views, each with a right-aligned count; the active one is filled, not outlined. (2) FILTERS: the rqt-sel field stack, one per dimension, label left, current value right, chevron, with a clear x once a field is set; menus portal to .ash so they escape the rail's scroll. (3) SORT: the same field plus the direction toggle underneath. (4) Foot: 'Clear filters', shown only when something is set, and 'Save as default' with its saved state.

Behaviour. The rail owns every filter. Nothing filters from the toolbar, from band tiles or from a chip row. Chips stay in the main column above the list, but purely as a read-out of what the rail is doing, each individually clearable. The main column's top row is fixed: view segmented tabs left, spacer, search, result count. Search never moves into the rail.

Phone, below 44rem. The rail becomes the existing rqt-sheet bottom sheet, opened by a Filters button carrying a count badge, with Clear all, Save as default and 'Show N' in the foot. Never a horizontal scroller of view chips, which is what invoices-studio does today.

Save default. One shared store, one key per page, so 'Save as default' means the same thing on every surface.

Pages that must adopt it. Leads, Calls, Deals, Proposals, Contracts, Schedules, Templates, Time, Team, Capacity, Tracks, Notifications, studio Files, portal Requests, portal Invoices, portal Files, invoices-studio, and the 13 placeholder pages the moment they are built. Bake it into the stub so nobody ships another toolbar.

Exemptions, written down so nobody re-litigates them. Messages, both audiences: two-pane master/detail, the left pane is the conversation list. The sales-artifacts builders and every detail page: no list to filter. Studio Overview and portal Overview: dashboards. Portal Account and Settings: tab pages. Portal Services: a catalogue with sections. Files is NOT exempt; its 15rem folder column becomes the rail's VIEWS section.

The editors' right-hand outline rail keeps its side, because it is a document outline and not a filter, but it adopts the rail's section header, item and count styling so the two read as one family rather than two products."
